<reason>A opened with the intuitive and strong physics/prevention frame (speed-survival curve, self-enforcing geometry, certainty over severity) and kept one live asymmetry alive throughout: punishment requires a prior catch, geometry requires nothing of the driver. But B reframed the debate twice in ways A never fully closed. First, the incapacitation reframe (interlock, revocation, impoundment as "physically self-enforcing" penalties that travel with the person) turned A's own physics standard against it; B's rejoinder that redesign is also triggered by a first victim, but then covers only forty feet of asphalt while a sanction covers the whole network, was the cleanest comparative move in the debate. Second, B's coverage-and-marginal-cost argument survived pressure: A's Q2 attempt to symmetrize buildout costs was answered directly and plausibly (courts, DMV, points system are sunk assets; a statutory change takes effect citywide immediately, versus pouring concrete block by block). B's pressure questions also did real damage: asked what the "lower limit" half delivers alone, A conceded it only bites when it triggers engineering, and then named speed cameras — letting B characterize A's fastest citywide tool as "enforcement wearing a hard hat." A's closing distinction (cameras are pre-crash, low-severity, limit-enforcing, not post-crash courtroom sanctions) is legitimate and partially repairs the damage, but it arrives late and after B had already extracted the frame. A also left its strongest theoretical weapon underused: its own certainty-over-severity claim cuts against *harsher* penalties specifically, and B's general-deterrence answer leaned on existing penalty levels rather than increased severity — A never sharpened that inconsistency. Both sides kept clean format and answered with A1:/A2:. B made the decision easier by supplying a single decisive metric (coverage/portability versus fixed geometry) and defending it under direct fire.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's [B2.1]-[B2.3] and [B4.5]-[B4.7]: recasting redesign as equally reactive (high-injury networks are rebuilt after deaths) while noting a sanction follows the driver everywhere, then converting A's own concession about speed cameras and "paint" into proof that the lower-limit half of the motion only bites when a consequence stands behind it.</best_rebuttal>
